title: Audio Volume applet cause excessive CPU usage when visible, especially when on the Desktop
line: The Audio Volume widget on the desktop no longer records every audio device while windows cover it.
explanation: Each volume slider runs a level meter (a PulseAudio record stream per device) whenever the slider is visible. In the tray that stops when the popup closes, but a widget on the desktop is always visible as far as Qt knows, so it kept recording every device and using CPU even when windows hid it completely, and no applet had a way to know it was hidden. libplasma now gives applets an obscured property; the desktop containment sets it for each widget while the windows on its screen, desktop and activity cover the widget together, following the widget's position on screen as it is moved or the layout shifts; the Audio Volume sliders stop their meters while their applet is obscured.

commits.message:
plasmaquick: add an obscured property to applets

Applets had no way to know they can't be seen, so a desktop widget kept
running live meters and animations under windows. Containments can now
mark an applet as obscured, and applets can pause such work while it is.

BUG: 441555

containments/desktop: mark applets covered by windows as obscured

Widgets on the desktop always counted as visible, even when windows hid
them completely. The desktop now tracks the windows on its screen and
marks each applet as obscured while they cover it, wherever it is moved.

BUG: 441555

applet: pause volume meters while the applet is obscured

A widget on the desktop is always visible as far as Qt knows, so its
level meters kept recording every device even when windows hid it. The
sliders now also stop their meters while the applet is obscured.

BUG: 441555

patches.diff:
From f5357b0bed5383f15da1c8342cb744c01d665d21 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 18:14:28 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] applet: pause volume meters while the applet is obscured

A widget on the desktop is always visible as far as Qt knows, so its
level meters kept recording every device even when windows hid it. The
sliders now also stop their meters while the applet is obscured.

BUG: 441555
---
 applet/VolumeSlider.qml | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/applet/VolumeSlider.qml b/applet/VolumeSlider.qml
index 5f365ccb..2f8d8929 100644
--- a/applet/VolumeSlider.qml
+++ b/applet/VolumeSlider.qml
@@ -35,7 +35,7 @@ PC3.Slider {
 
     VolumeMonitor {
         id: meter
-        target: control.visible && control.showVolumeIndicator ? control.volumeObject : null
+        target: control.visible && control.showVolumeIndicator && !main.obscured ? control.volumeObject : null
     }
 
     Behavior on volume {
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: Master: Dolphin and Konsole together cover the desktop Audio Volume widget while a sound plays; the widget still keeps 2 level meter record streams open
With the fix, same two windows: the widget is obscured and has no meter streams open
Master: the widget's top edge shows above Konsole (left); moving the panel to the top shifts the widget fully under the window (right), and both keep 2 meter streams
With the fix: 2 meter streams while part of the widget shows (left), 0 once the layout shift moves it fully under the window (right)

review.text: Clean layering: a generic AppletQuickItem.obscured property in libplasma, set by the desktop containment from libtaskmanager window geometries (the same source the panel already uses for dodge/opacity), and a one-line read in plasma-pa's VolumeSlider, so the meters actually stop instead of being hidden behind a setting. The rectangle subtraction handles jointly covering windows, and its failure modes (skip-taskbar windows ignored, translucent windows counted as covering) only err toward the current behaviour or toward not drawing meters nobody can see clearly. Media and verification show 2 -> 0 meter streams under two windows, after layout shifts and drags, and recovery on uncover, Peek at Desktop and minimize. Minor polish maintainers may ask for: only activate the TasksModel Loader when the containment actually holds applets, so plain desktops don't pay for window tracking.
